title: burst-aware-kv-cache-prefetch-profiling
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of experiments exploring how kv-cache prefetch granularity interacts with multi-GPU comm subsystems (NCCL/NVLink/PCIe) and how that coupling produces microbursts/tail-latency in TP/PP inference. This is an exploratory sketch — notes, traces, config knobs, and actionable heuristics at the end.

Background / motivation:
- Runtime prefetch pulls KV pages ahead of token generation to avoid stalls for long contexts. Prefetch can be buttoned to different granularities: per-layer, per-block, per-chunk.
- On multi-GPU setups with tensor/pipeline parallel shards, prefetch causes synchronized PCIe/NVLink transfers across replicas. Under certain patterns this creates brief but heavy network bursts that push NCCL out of its smoothing envelope and increase p95/p99.
- We saw customer reports of intermittent 50–200ms spikes on otherwise healthy 8xA100 nodes when using aggressive prefetch + small batch size.

Testbed:
- Nodes: 4x8xA100-PCIE (NVIDIA driver 535), dual-socket hosts. NVLink mesh inside GPU box, PCIe to CPU.
- NCCL 2.18.3, libnccl tuned via NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL and NCCL_ALGO=Ring (default), NCCL_SHM_ENABLE=1.
- Models: 33B dense (TP=2, PP=4), and a 7B long-context (TP=1, PP=8) for contrast.
- Workloads: synthetic chat-style requests with variable prefix lengths (avg 256 tokens, tails up to 2k), batch sizes 1/2/4, streaming generate at 1 token per 10ms host scheduling.
- Instrumentation: per-GPU nvprof-like traces (Nsight system), Prometheus traces (token-level latency), custom kernel-level timestamps in runtime for prefetch start/end, NCCL timeline via NCCL_PROTO=VERSION env logging.

Knobs tried:
- Prefetch granularity: chunk sizes = {1 layer, 2 layers, 4 layers, full-block}.
- Prefetch policy: sync (blocking) vs async (fire-and-forget) vs staggered (offset per replica by microseconds).
- Network smoothing: host staging window (0, 8, 32 ms), small transfer coalescing on host side (merge small PCIe reads).
- NCCL pacing: NCCL_NSOCKS_PERTHREAD adjustments, NCCL_COLLNET options where applicable.

Key observations:
1) Aggressive per-layer prefetch (small chunks) -> many tiny transfers that align across replicas -> narrow high-rate bursts on NVLink/PCIe. On the TP/PP 2x4 setup, bursts coincide with PP token handoff causing NCCL ring re-entrancy, p95 increases by ~3–4x, p99 by 6–8x relative to baseline.
2) Larger chunk prefetch (4 layers or whole-block) reduces number of DMA ops and spreads bandwidth over longer windows -> significantly reduces spike amplitude but increases average transfer size; tradeoff: more host memory pressure and occasional single larger stall if transfer gets delayed.
3) Async prefetch + staggered offsets across replicas reduces burst alignment and smooths traffic. The best result came from offsetting prefetch by a small jitter proportional to replica_id * (avg_kernel_time/8).
4) Host staging (batching small reads before issuing PCIe DMA) further smoothed bursts, but this increases wall-clock prefetch latency and needs an informed timeout to avoid stalling critical small transfers.
5) NCCL behavior: when bursts produced high packet rates, NCCL reverted to extra retransmits and collective retries. NCCL logs showed transient queue saturation and increased cudaMemcpy latency. Tuning NCCL_SHM_ENABLE and increasing ring buffer sizes helped marginally but did not eliminate the problem.

Metrics excerpt (example):
- Baseline (prefetch per-block): p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=120ms.
- Aggressive per-layer: p50=14ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms.
- Async staggered + host staging: p50=13ms, p95=55ms, p99=140ms.

Traces / signals to watch in prod:
- Short sharp spikes in PCIe/NVLink utilization (high instantaneous bandwidth for <10ms).
- NCCL retransmit / queue-full messages.
- Simultaneous start timestamps for prefetch across GPUs.
- Correlated increases in kernel queuing latency right after prefetch windows.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Default prefetch policy: use chunk sizes >= 2 layers for TP/PP topologies by default, with autoscaling adjusting to model layer runtimes.
2) Stagger prefetch start by replica id with small jitter (1–5% of avg layer time). Implemented as deterministic offset to keep more reproducible behavior for debugging.
3) Provide a host-staging buffer that collects tiny reads for up to 8–16ms or until N bytes threshold reached, whichever comes first. Expose knobs and sensible defaults.
4) Add runtime telemetry: emit prefetch windows and per-GPU transfer histograms to console/Prometheus so customers can correlate tail-latency events.
5) NCCL: expose adaptive ring-buffer tuning and surface a suggestion profile for affected hardware (we will collect per-cluster recommendations).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Vary NVLink topologies (islanded vs full-mesh) — how does islanding change optimal chunk sizes? We only tested full-mesh.
- Interaction with KV cache eviction: if prefetch triggers eviction thrashing, tail latency might worsen due to repeated large transfers. Need an experiment coupling eviction policy changes.
- Test on DGX/Multi-node RDMA setups (0-hop vs 1-hop) to see if RDMA semantics reduce bursts.
- Evaluate finer NCCL pacing features (COLLNET/PROTO tweaks) and newer NCCL versions.

Implementation notes for runtime PR:
- Add PrefetchConfig: {chunk_layers:int, max_batch_ms:int, stagger_us:int, host_stage_thresh_bytes:int}. Default: chunk_layers=2, max_batch_ms=12, stagger_us=replica_id*(avg_layer_ms/8).
- Instrumentation: emit timestamps for prefetch:{start,end}, host_stage:{flush,start} and NCCL:{collective_start,end} with token_id and request_id.

Links / artifacts:
- Jira: RW-3412 (customer tail-latency report)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289 (prefetch prototype)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is exploratory and contains raw numbers from lab runs. Before rolling defaults to customers, we should run a 2-week soak on nightly cluster with a mix of models and customer-like traffic.
- We should capture full NCCL timeline snapshots for at least two representative racks to produce cluster-level tuning recommendations.

Action items:
- [ ] Aisha: add host-stage buffer implementation in prefetch branch (PR linked).
- [ ] Ravi: run islanded NVLink test on rack B (slot 3–6) and upload traces.
- [ ] Daniel: prepare a telemetry dashboard prototype showing prefetch windows and per-GPU instantaneous bandwidth for the console.

End of note.
